title: Measurement chips and arrow captions stay crisp when you zoom in
goal: When you zoom past 100 percent the labels you place are now drawn sharp, but the numbers on a measurement, the caption on an arrow and the strokes of a shape are still blown up from a document-sized picture, so they go soft next to sharp text. Everything drawn from shapes and type should be as sharp as the text is.
notes: Follow-up to the crisp-zoom work of 2026-09-04. DocumentRenderer.renderTile already magnifies the document and rasterizes text at the tile scale; MeasureRasterizer, AnnotationRasterizer and CollageRasterizer are still called with the document-point box and magnified afterwards (see the boxInPoints branch in ciImage(for:)). Each one needs the same treatment TextRasterizer got: a scale parameter that scales the CGContext, leaving the geometry in document points. Watch the raster cache keys.
acceptance: A measurement chip placed at 100 percent is still sharp at 400 percent zoom
An arrow caption pill is still sharp at 400 percent zoom
A shape stroke and its layer border are still crisp at 400 percent zoom
The 12 megapixel ten layer crisp tile benchmark stays under 16ms
